exact_statement: For every Boolean function F on at most six independent uniform physical bits and every distinguished pair A of bits such that each positive-probability conditional spectral law of S_(A^c) given S_A is a product law, H(F)<=Cstar I(F), where Cstar=16/3-(3/2)log2(3). The constant is attained by a three-variable point defect containing both addresses, with remaining coordinates dummy. On the subclass in which every physical data point has exactly one nonzero partial address Fourier slice (pure configurations), H(F)<=12I(F)/5, attained with four essential variables. On the subclass with all four slices of magnitude1/2 at every data point, H(F)<=2I(F) in every data dimension. A normalized non-Boolean product spectrum with six marginals1/16 has H/I>4, so the finite Boolean bound is not generic probability algebra.
hypotheses: F is a real Boolean sign on a finite uniform physical cube
A consists of two distinct physical coordinates
Conditional squared Fourier spectra are product laws; zero-mass address labels omitted
Full finite bound requires at most six variables; the all-mixed bound is explicitly dimension-independent
H is in bits; I is total physical influence, equivalently expected spectral degree
